record.context_brief: Full main term for the eighth moment
record.original_question: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis and a smoothed quaternary additive divisor conjecture. Starting from the conjectured asymptotic I4(T) ~ C4 T (log T)^16 for the eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function, derive the full main term up to an error of size o(T) or a power saving, obtain a shifted analogue, and asymptotically evaluate the smoothed shifted integral of product_{j=1}^4 zeta(1/2 + a_j + it) zeta(1/2 + b_j - it) when |a_j| and |b_j| are << 1/log T and omega is supported in [c1 T, c2 T].

evidence.quote: Under the same assumptions, obtain the full main term, up to an error term of size o(T ) or a power savings error term. Obtain a shifted version of this result. Under the same assumptions, asymptotically evaluate integral omega(t) product_{j=1}^4 zeta(1/2 + a_j + it) zeta(1/2 + b_j - it) dt where a_j, b_j are complex numbers satisfying |a_j|, |b_j| << 1/log T.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function. Define the eighth moment

$$I_4(T) = \int_0^T \left|\zeta\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+it\right)\right|^8\,dt.$$

Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. For an integer $k\ge 1$, the smoothed $k$-fold (quaternary when $k=4$) additive divisor conjecture asserts an asymptotic formula with power-saving error for sums of the form
$$\sum_n d_k(n)\,d_k(n+h)\,W(n/N),$$
where $d_k$ is the $k$-fold divisor function, $W$ is a fixed smooth compactly supported test function, and $h$ is a non-zero integer with $|h|\ll N^{1-\delta}$, the asymptotic being uniform in $h$ with explicit main term given by a polynomial of degree $2k-2$ in $\log N$.

Under the Riemann Hypothesis and the smoothed quaternary ($k=4$) additive divisor conjecture, complete the following three tasks:

(a) Refine the asymptotic
$$I_4(T) \sim C_4\, T\,(\log T)^{16}$$
to a full main term, i.e. produce an explicit polynomial $P_{16}(x)$ of degree $16$ such that
$$I_4(T) = T\,P_{16}(\log T) + E(T),$$
where $E(T) = o(T)$, or, more strongly, $E(T) \ll T^{1-\eta}$ for some fixed $\eta>0$.

(b) Establish the shifted analogue: for complex shifts $a,b$ with $|a|,|b|\ll 1/\log T$, obtain an asymptotic with main term and a comparable error for
$$\int_0^T \left|\zeta\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+a+it\right)\right|^4 \left|\zeta\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+b+it\right)\right|^4 dt$$
and, more generally, for the shifted eighth moment with four independent shifts.

(c) Let $\omega:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a fixed smooth function supported in $[c_1 T,\,c_2 T]$ for fixed constants $0<c_1<c_2$, and let $a_1,\dots,a_4,b_1,\dots,b_4\in\mathbb{C}$ satisfy $|a_j|,|b_j|\ll 1/\log T$. Asymptotically evaluate, with main term predicted by the recipe of Conrey–Farmer–Keating–Rubinstein–Snaith and an error term that is $o\!\left(\int\omega\right)$ or a power saving in $T$, the integral
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}} \omega(t)\,\prod_{j=1}^{4}\zeta\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+a_j+it\right)\zeta\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+b_j-it\right)\,dt.$$
artifact.category_tag: moments of the Riemann zeta function
artifact.status_search_result: The unconditional/conditional asymptotic $I_4(T)\sim C_4 T(\log T)^{16}$ has been established (under RH and a quaternary additive divisor conjecture). Refining this to a full degree-16 main term polynomial with $o(T)$ or power-saving error, and establishing the corresponding shifted eighth moment asymptotic with arbitrary shifts of size $\ll 1/\log T$, are stated as open problems. No subsequent paper appears to fully resolve them as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: The eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes an asymptotic formula for the eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function, assuming the Riemann hypothesis and a quaternary additive divisor conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Only the leading-order asymptotic is established; full main term with power-saving error remains open.

status_evidence.title: Moments of L-functions Problem List
status_evidence.snippet: Problem list cataloguing open questions on moments of L-functions, including obtaining the full main term and shifted analogue of the eighth moment.
status_evidence.claim: The full main term, shifted version, and shifted CFKRS-type integral evaluation are listed as open problems.
